title: Substitutionary Atonement
definition: Substitutionary Atonement is Christ's work of standing in the place of sinners, bearing their guilt, and dying for their sins.
summary: Jesus saves by taking the sinner's place under judgment.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lamb of God who bears sin and gives His life for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Substitutionary Atonement helps explain how God saves sinners through Jesus Christ rather than through human merit, religious performance, or self-rescue. This doctrine shows that salvation is personal, covenantal, and centered on the finished work of Christ.

Scripture presents this truth so believers can understand the grace they have received and proclaim the Gospel with clarity. It guards the Church from confusion by keeping sin, grace, faith, repentance, righteousness, forgiveness, and eternal hope in their biblical order.

The heart of this doctrine is jesus saves by taking the sinner's place under judgment.. It should lead to worship, assurance, humility, holiness, and a deeper confidence in the Savior who saves completely.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people easily drift toward either despair or self-righteousness. Substitutionary Atonement reminds believers that salvation belongs to the Lord, rests in Christ, and produces real transformation without turning grace into license or obedience into a way to earn acceptance with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive this truth with humility and examine whether your hope is resting in Christ. Let substitutionary atonement shape your prayers, your witness, your repentance, and your daily confidence that Jesus is able to save and keep all who come to God through Him.
